requirements.statement: `shogun stats --json` prints, instead of the table and totals text, one JSON document on stdout containing one object per run and a totals object.

criteria.text: With --json, stdout parses as exactly one JSON document and contains neither the table header "RUN\tSTATUS" nor the "total:" line.

Each readable run object has id, status, mode, planner, reviewer, attempts, active_seconds, input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost_usd and usage with the same values the table shows (active time in seconds, unrounded).
A damaged run object has status "damaged" and its damage reason in a damaged field.

The totals object has the run count, runs by status, damaged count, attempts, active_seconds, the five token sums, cost_usd, the incomplete/unknown usage counts, and booleans telling whether spend (attempts, time) and usage (tokens, cost) totals are lower bounds, matching the text totals' 'at least' rules.

approach.summary: Add a `json` bool flag in cmdStats. Keep the existing loop that accumulates totals, but skip the tabwriter writes when --json is set, and collect one row struct per run instead. After the loop, in JSON mode, build a totals struct from the values already computed (tot, byStatus, damaged, partial, and the two 'at least' conditions), marshal {runs, totals} with json.MarshalIndent(…, "", " "), print it with Fprintln and return. The text path is left byte-for-byte as it is. Update the usage line and the README row, and extend the existing test with a --json run on the same fixture.

steps.title: Add --json output to cmdStats
steps.objective: `shogun stats --json` prints runs and totals as one JSON document; the text output stays the same.
actions: In stats.go import "encoding/json". After the --dir flag add `asJSON := fs.Bool("json", false, "print runs and totals as JSON on stdout")`.

Define two small types next to runStats. statsRow has json tags: id, status, damaged (omitempty string), and an embedded *statsCounts pointer. statsCounts holds mode, planner, reviewer, attempts, active_seconds, input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost_usd and usage, with no omitempty, so zeros stay visible. It is nil for a damaged run, so those fields are left out. statsTotals holds runs, by_status (map[string]int), damaged, attempts, active_seconds, the five token sums, cost_usd, usage_incomplete_runs, usage_unknown_runs, spend_lower_bound and usage_lower_bound.

In the existing loop, guard each fmt.Fprintf(tw, …) (the header line too) with `if !*asJSON`. Append a statsRow per run: for a damaged run {id, "damaged", r.damaged, nil}; for a readable run {id, string(r.st.Status), "", &statsCounts{mode, r.planner, r.reviewer, counters…, u}}. Keep the accumulation of tot, byStatus, damaged and partial unchanged.

After the loop, if *asJSON: build statsTotals from len(runs), byStatus, damaged, tot, partial["incomplete"] and partial["unknown"]; set spend_lower_bound = damaged > 0 and usage_lower_bound = len(partial) > 0 || damaged > 0. Marshal struct{Runs []statsRow `json:"runs"`; Totals statsTotals `json:"totals"`} with json.MarshalIndent(v, "", " "), Fprintln it to a.stdout and return ExitOK. Otherwise continue into the unchanged tw.Flush() and totals text. The empty-runs early return (stderr message) stays as it is (see Q-001).
Update the stats usage line in main.go:87 to `shogun stats [--dir d] [--json]` and keep the alignment. In README.md:237 append `, `--json`` after `--dir` in the stats row.

verification.expected: `go build ./... && go vet ./cmd/shogun` succeed and gofmt -l cmd/shogun prints nothing.
git diff of stats.go shows no changes to the header string, the row format strings or the totals Fprintf lines; they are only wrapped in `if !*asJSON` or come after the JSON early return.

risks.risk: Guarding the header/row writes incorrectly could change or drop text output.
